setting: A co-op AI teammate (a bot) in a tactical shooter like Rainbow Six Siege or Counter-Strike. The human player places markers on the map (a pin, a ping, a mark) and gives voice orders in English. The voice goes through speech-to-text; the bot receives the transcript (and, separately, the latest marker position). The bot must map each transcript to exactly one intent below; its planner then works out how to carry it out (which window, which route, where the marker is). Words like 'here', 'there', 'that', 'this' usually refer to the latest marker or to where the player is looking; the planner resolves them. The same game also has farming and building, on the same map and at the same time as the fighting: the bot can be told to plant, water and harvest crops, prepare the ground, feed animals, collect produce and materials, carry things somewhere, and build, repair or take down pieces from its build menu. A line is read with every intent available; nothing tells the bot which kind of work the player has in mind except the line itself.

intents.FOLLOW_ME: the bot follows the player and stays with them. 'Look at me' is LOOK_AT_ME: the bot turns, it does not come. 'Come back' / 'come back to me' is COME_BACK; 'go back' / 'return' is GO_BACK
intents.MOVE_TO: the bot moves to a place: the marker, or a named or pointed-at location (a door, stairs, a floor, the roof). If the player says to jump, drop, hop or climb ('jump down', 'climb up on that') it is JUMP. Going or getting inside something with no word about clearing it ('go inside', 'get in there', 'get inside the box', 'crawl into the vent') is this intent too: the bot just goes in. Coming back to the player ('come back', 'come back to me') is COME_BACK; going back to where the bot was ('go back', 'return') is GO_BACK. Going to get an item is this intent, and the item is the place: 'go find ammo', 'get some ammo', 'grab a gun', 'find a weapon', 'pick up that rifle', 'go get health' (the nearest place that gives it). Going to a car is this intent ('go to the car'); getting into it is GET_IN. Going up or down with no particular place, or by a way the line names without singling one out ('go up', 'go up by the stairs', 'take the steps up', 'go down the ramp', 'head down', 'find a way up'), is this intent: the planner takes the nearest way that way, the one the player looks at first. Going inside with no place named ('go inside', 'get indoors', 'get in the building') is this intent with the zone 'inside'. Taking out a weapon the bot already carries ('switch to your pistol', 'use your rifle', 'pull out your sidearm') is SWITCH_WEAPON; reloading is RELOAD. Going on with a movement that names its way, side or place is this intent with that way ('keep moving forward', 'keep going left', 'continue up the stairs', 'carry on forward', 'further up', 'more down', 'a bit further forward', 'and up'); 'advance' and 'keep advancing' are this intent forward. A going-on that names none ('keep moving', 'keep going', 'continue', 'continue moving') is NONE. Gathering produce or materials ('collect the eggs', 'chop some wood') is COLLECT and carrying something somewhere ('bring the wood here') is DELIVER; going to the field, the barn or the greenhouse is this intent. Going into or through a teleport or a portal ('go into the portal', 'take the teleport', 'go through the teleporter') is this intent: the teleport is the place
intents.HOLD_POSITION: the bot stays where it is and stops moving. With a place or the player's marker the bot goes there and stays: 'stay at my pin', 'stay on my mark', 'stay over there' are this intent, and the target or the reference says where. Only changing posture is CROUCH / PRONE / STAND_UP. Waiting at a place is staying there: 'wait here', 'wait there', 'wait right here', 'wait for me here', 'wait at the north door' are this intent; a bare 'wait' or 'wait for it' is WAIT. 'Don't move' is this intent too. Standing at a place is staying there: 'stand here', 'stand there', 'stand right here', 'stand on my pin', 'stand at the north door' are this intent ('go stand by the window', with a verb of going, is MOVE_TO; 'stand up' is STAND_UP). 'Dig in' (stay put) is this intent; digging the ground is TILL
intents.HOLD_ANGLE: the bot watches a specific angle / door / window / corridor / stairs, ready to shoot, and keeps watching it. Only turning to look at something is LOOK_AT. It stays this intent when the player says they take the other one themselves ('hold this angle, I'll take the other one')
intents.HOLD_OTHER_ANGLE: the bot watches the OTHER angle than the one currently covered (by the player or by the bot), e.g. the player takes one door and tells the bot to take the other ('you take the other one', 'the other angle', 'another angle', 'the opposite side'). What counts is which angle the BOT gets: 'hold this angle, I'll take the other one' leaves the bot on its angle and is HOLD_ANGLE
intents.FLANK: the bot takes an alternative route around to hit the enemy from the side or behind, often via the marker
intents.VAULT_WINDOW: the bot goes in or out through a WINDOW (vault, climb, jump or hop through it; a bare 'vault' or 'vault in' means the window). Jumping, dropping or climbing that is not through a window ('jump down', 'hop over the sofa') is JUMP. 'Hop in' / 'jump in' with no window named is GET_IN (a vehicle)
intents.RAPPEL: the bot uses a rappel rope on the outside of the building (rappel, rope up, rope down, drop down on the rope, hang at a window). Just going to a named place, the roof included, is MOVE_TO; jumping or dropping down with no rope in the wording ('drop down', 'jump off the roof') is JUMP. A ramp is walked, not roped: 'go down the ramp', 'take the ramp up' are MOVE_TO
intents.BREACH: the bot opens a wall, floor hatch, ceiling or barricaded door with a breaching charge or tool (loud). Taking down a structure without going through it ('tear down the fence', 'demolish the shed') is DEMOLISH
intents.DRONE: the bot sends a drone or another gadget, or scouts ahead, to gather intel before anyone goes in. 'Check that room' with no drone and no scouting word is CHECK
intents.FLASH: the bot throws a flashbang / stun grenade
intents.SMOKE: the bot throws a smoke grenade
intents.FRAG: the bot throws a lethal grenade (frag, molotov, incendiary)
intents.COVER_ME: the bot covers the PLAYER (watches over them, ready to shoot) while the player moves or does something. 'Covering fire' and 'suppressing fire' are SUPPRESS. The player reloading is no order to reload: 'cover me, I'm reloading' is this intent. 'Cover me while I build / plant / harvest' is this intent: the player does the work
intents.ENTRY: the bot pushes into the room / site and clears it. A bare 'attack' that names no way is ATTACK; 'check the room' is CHECK. Just going or getting inside, with no pushing or clearing in the wording ('go inside', 'get in there'), is MOVE_TO. Clearing a field of weeds or rocks is TILL
intents.FALL_BACK: the bot retreats / breaks off from the fight. 'Come back' with no retreat in the wording is COME_BACK; 'go back' and 'return' are GO_BACK. Getting out of a vehicle ('get out of the car', 'hop out') is GET_OUT; 'get out of there' / 'get out of the fight' is this intent; a bare 'get out' is GET_OUT
intents.PLANT: the bot plants the bomb / defuser. Planting a crop, seeds or seedlings is PLANT_CROP ('plant the carrots', 'sow the field'); a bare 'plant' with nothing named stays this intent
intents.DEFUSE: the bot defuses the bomb / disables the defuser
intents.HELP_INTERACTION: the player is stuck, trapped, or locked in or out, and asks the bot to get them out or let them through (let me out, let me in, get me out of here, I'm stuck in here, I'm locked in, help me get out, I can't get out), or asks the bot to work something for them that they cannot reach or use themselves (press the button for me, pull the lever, hit the switch for me). The bot comes to the player and does it. Opening a door or a window as an order of its own ('open the door', 'open it for me') is OPEN; help with nothing named is HELP
intents.WAIT: the bot pauses: stop what you are doing, hold up, do not act yet, cancel the last order. Only stopping the shooting is HOLD_FIRE. A bare 'no' that answers the bot is NO. A negated order is this intent: the bot stops and waits ('don't breach', 'don't follow me', 'don't go there', 'don't jump down', 'no need to check'). Only 'don't shoot' / 'don't fire' is HOLD_FIRE and 'don't move' is HOLD_POSITION. Waiting at a place ('wait here', 'wait there', 'wait at the door') is HOLD_POSITION
intents.GO_NOW: the bot executes the prepared or announced action right now; the player's go signal. A bare 'yes' that answers the bot is YES
intents.TAKE_COVER: the bot gets ITSELF into cover or out of sight to protect itself (hide, get behind something solid, get down); its planner picks the spot: the nearest cover, or the marker if the player points at one. Protecting the player is COVER_ME, not this. Only changing posture where the bot stands ('crouch', 'lie down', 'go prone') is CROUCH / PRONE. Building cover ('build some cover here', 'put up a barricade') is BUILD
intents.OPEN: the bot opens a door, window, hatch, gate or shutter the normal way (by hand, quietly) and does NOT go through it; its planner picks which one. Going through a window is VAULT_WINDOW, pushing into the room is ENTRY, forcing it open with a charge or tool is BREACH. 'Let me out', 'let me in', 'get me out of here' is HELP_INTERACTION: the player is stuck and the bot frees them
intents.ATTACK: the bot attacks the enemy, and HOW is left to its planner (push in, breach, or shoot from where it is): the player only says to attack / engage / take them out and names no way. If the player names the way, it is that intent instead: pushing into a room is ENTRY, a charge is BREACH, a grenade is FRAG, opening fire is OPEN_FIRE. Telling the bot to kill ITSELF ('kill yourself', 'go die') is KILL_YOURSELF
intents.OPEN_FIRE: the bot starts shooting, or is told it is free to shoot (open fire, start shooting, weapons free, fire at will, light them up); its planner picks the targets. A place or direction in the line is where to shoot. Suppressive or covering fire is SUPPRESS
intents.HOLD_FIRE: the bot stops shooting or must not start (hold fire, cease fire, check fire, don't shoot, stop shooting), also until something happens ('don't shoot until they come closer'). It is an order even though it is phrased as a negation. The bot may keep moving and doing other things: pausing everything is WAIT. 'Check fire' / 'check your fire' is radio wording for stop shooting: this intent, not CHECK
intents.LOOK_AT: the bot turns and looks at something: a named place or object, the thing the player points at, or a direction (look at the sofa, look at that window, look left, look up, look behind you, face the door, turn around). It is one look, not a watch: keeping an angle covered, ready to shoot, is HOLD_ANGLE ('watch the window', 'eyes on the door', 'cover the stairs'); going to a place is MOVE_TO, checking a place or a side ('check that room', 'check your six') is CHECK. A 'look' that is not about turning to see is not this intent: a warning or an exclamation ('look out', 'look at that shot'), a filler ('look, we need to move'), searching ('look for the defuser') are NONE. Asking whether the bot sees something ('do you see that?', 'can you see him?') is SEE_THING: a question, not a turn
intents.LOOK_AT_ME: the bot turns and looks at the PLAYER (look at me, face me, turn to me, look over here). The bot does not come to the player -- that is FOLLOW_ME -- and does not start covering them (COVER_ME). Asking whether the bot sees the player ('do you see me?') is SEE_ME
intents.HELP: the player asks the bot for help and does not say with what (help me, help me here, I need a hand, I need backup here), or asks to be revived or picked up when down (revive me, I'm down, pick me up, help me up). The bot comes to the player and its planner works out what is needed. If the player says what they need, it is that intent: being let out, let in or freed, or having a control worked for them, is HELP_INTERACTION ('let me out', 'get me out of here', 'press the button for me'); being covered is COVER_ME, being followed is FOLLOW_ME. Help with a named job is that job ('help me harvest the wheat' is HARVEST, 'help me build the wall' is BUILD)
intents.CHECK: the bot checks a place or a thing itself: goes and looks whether it is clear or what is there, and how is left to its planner (check that room, check the basement, check behind the sofa, check your six, see if it's clear, make sure nobody is in there). With a drone or another gadget it is DRONE; pushing in to clear the room by force is ENTRY; only turning to look is LOOK_AT; keeping it covered is HOLD_ANGLE. 'Check fire' / 'check your fire' is the order to stop shooting: HOLD_FIRE, but checking a place whose name has the word is this intent ('check the fire escape', 'check the fire exit'). 'Do you see anything there?' asked of the bot where it is, is SEE_THING; going to see is this intent ('go see if it's clear')
intents.SUPPRESS: the bot lays down suppressive fire: keeps shooting at a place or at the enemy to pin them down, not to pick targets (suppress, suppressive fire, suppress them, covering fire, pin them down, keep their heads down). A plain order to start shooting is OPEN_FIRE; watching over the player without the order to shoot is COVER_ME
intents.JUMP: the bot jumps, drops or climbs with its own body -- no rope, and not through a window: down from where it is (off a ledge, a roof edge, a balcony, through an open hatch or a hole in the floor), up onto something, over an obstacle, across a gap (jump down, drop down, hop over that, jump on the table, climb up there, jump off the roof). Through a window it is VAULT_WINDOW; on a rope it is RAPPEL; walking down the stairs or just going to a place is MOVE_TO ('go down', 'head downstairs'); 'get down' in the sense of ducking or hiding is TAKE_COVER. Going, getting or climbing INSIDE something ('get inside the vent', 'climb into the box') is MOVE_TO; jumping or dropping in is still this intent ('jump into the hole', 'drop in through the hatch'). Jumping into a vehicle ('jump in the car') is GET_IN
intents.COME_BACK: the bot comes back to the PLAYER (come back, come back here, come back to me, get back here, get back to me, back to me, return to me, regroup, rejoin me). Going back to where the bot itself was is GO_BACK ('go back', 'return', 'return to your position', 'head back'); retreating from a fight is FALL_BACK ('fall back', 'pull back', 'get back'); coming to the player or staying with them is FOLLOW_ME ('come here', 'on me', 'come with me'); going back to a place the line names is MOVE_TO ('go back to the stairs'). Going on coming back ('keep coming', 'keep coming back', 'keep coming this way') is this intent; 'keep coming closer' is FOLLOW_ME, as 'come closer'
intents.CROUCH: the bot crouches or stays low where it is: a change of posture on the spot (crouch, crouch down, get low, stay low, squat, take a knee, sit down). Getting into cover is TAKE_COVER ('get down', 'duck', 'hide')
intents.PRONE: the bot lies down flat where it is (lie down, lay down, go prone, get on the ground, on your belly, hit the deck). 'Lay down fire' is SUPPRESS; getting into cover is TAKE_COVER
intents.STAND_UP: the bot stands up from crouching or lying (stand up, get up, on your feet, get back up). 'Get me up' / 'help me up' is HELP; 'get up on that' and 'get up there' are JUMP or MOVE_TO; 'stand still', 'stand here' are HOLD_POSITION 'Stand on my pin', 'stand by the door' are HOLD_POSITION too
intents.YES: the player answers yes to something the bot asked, or confirms what the bot said (yes, yeah, yep, affirmative, correct, that's right, exactly, sure, okay as a bare answer). It is not an order: the bot's planner uses it only if it asked something. If the line also gives an order, it is that order ('yes, breach it' = BREACH; 'yes, go' = GO_NOW). 'Roger' / 'copy' / 'got it' only acknowledge and are NONE. Praise of what the bot did ('nice shot', 'good job', 'well done') is PRAISE; the bare word that answers the bot ('good', 'great', 'perfect') stays this intent
intents.NO: the player answers no, or rejects what the bot said or proposed (no, nope, nah, negative, wrong, not that one, that's not it). If the line also gives an order, it is that order ('no, hold fire' = HOLD_FIRE; 'no, wait' = WAIT). Pausing or cancelling an order is WAIT ('stop', 'hold on', 'cancel that', 'never mind'); a negated order is WAIT ('don't breach')
intents.MAYBE: the player's answer is neither yes nor no: it may be so, or the bot may decide (maybe, perhaps, possibly, could be, probably, I guess so, up to you, your call)
intents.DONT_KNOW: the player answers that they do not know (I don't know, no idea, not sure, dunno, can't tell, who knows). It is an answer even though it is phrased as a negation
intents.GET_IN: the bot gets into a vehicle: a car, a truck (get in the car, get into the car, go into the car, hop in, jump in the car, get in the truck, get in the vehicle, take the car). It takes a free seat, the driver's when that is the only one. Going into a room, a box, a vent or a building is MOVE_TO; through a window is VAULT_WINDOW; going TO the car without getting in ('go to the car', 'run to the truck') is MOVE_TO
intents.GET_OUT: the bot gets out of the vehicle it is in (get out of the car, hop out, jump out of the car, exit the vehicle, leave the car, out of the truck). A bare 'get out' (said to the bot in a car) is this intent too; with the bot in no vehicle the game takes it as falling back. 'Get out of there', 'get out of the fight', 'get out of his line' (leaving a place or a fight) is FALL_BACK
intents.REPEAT: the bot does again what it was told last, or the part of it that it could not do (try again, again, do it again, one more time, once more, repeat that, same again, go again, more, give it another go). An order said again with its own words is that order ('shoot again' is OPEN_FIRE, 'frag it again' is FRAG); 'one more on your left' is a callout (NONE)
intents.GO_BACK: the bot goes back to where IT was before the last order that moved it (go back, go back there, go back to where you were, return, head back, return to your position, back to your post, get back to your spot). The planner knows that place; the line names none. Coming back to the PLAYER is COME_BACK ('come back', 'come back to me', 'get back to me', 'get back here'); going back to a place the line names is MOVE_TO ('go back to the stairs', 'head back to the first floor'); retreating from a fight is FALL_BACK ('fall back', 'pull back')
intents.SWITCH_WEAPON: the bot changes the weapon in its hands for another one it carries (switch weapons, change weapon, swap guns, next weapon, switch to your pistol, pull out your sidearm, use your rifle, go to your shotgun, switch to primary). A weapon named is the one to take, if the bot has it; with none named the bot takes the next one it carries that has ammo. Picking up or going to get a weapon lying in the world is MOVE_TO ('grab that rifle', 'go get a shotgun', 'find a weapon', 'pick up the pistol by my pin'); putting a fresh magazine in the same weapon is RELOAD; shooting is OPEN_FIRE
intents.RELOAD: the bot reloads the weapon in its hands (reload, reload now, change mags, swap mags, new mag, top off, get a fresh mag in). The player saying THEY are reloading ('cover me, I'm reloading') is COVER_ME or whatever they ask for; going to find or pick up ammo is MOVE_TO ('go find ammo', 'grab some ammo'); taking another weapon is SWITCH_WEAPON
intents.PLANT_CROP: the bot plants or sows a crop: seeds, seedlings, bulbs, saplings, or a crop by name (plant carrots, sow the wheat, put the tomato seedlings in, plant some potatoes in that bed, seed the north field, put a sunflower here). What it plants is the item; where is the target (a field, a bed, a plot, a planter, the greenhouse, here, my pin). Planting the bomb or the defuser is PLANT; a bare 'plant it' / 'plant here' with no crop or seed named is PLANT too (the planner looks at what the bot carries)
intents.WATER: the bot waters plants or ground (water the carrots, water the north field, give the tomatoes some water, sprinkle the beds, water everything in the greenhouse). Fetching water or filling a can is COLLECT
intents.HARVEST: the bot harvests crops that grow in the ground or on plants (harvest the wheat, pick the tomatoes, dig up the potatoes, cut the corn, gather the strawberries, reap the field, pick the grapes). Taking eggs, honey, milk, wood or stone is COLLECT
intents.TILL: the bot prepares the ground for planting or keeps it clean: till, plow, hoe, rake, dig a bed, loosen the soil, weed, pull the weeds, clear the field of rocks or weeds, fertilize, spread manure. 'Clear the room' / 'clear the basement' (of enemies) stays ENTRY; 'dig in' (stay and hold) stays HOLD_POSITION
intents.FEED: the bot feeds animals (feed the chickens, give the cows some hay, fill the troughs, throw grain to the hens, feed the pigs). The item is the food, the target the animals or their pen
intents.COLLECT: the bot gathers produce or materials that are not crops in the ground and keeps them: collect the eggs, get the honey from the hives, milk the cow, shear the sheep, chop some wood, cut down that tree, mine stone, pick up the planks, grab the seeds from the shed, fill the watering can. Picking up a weapon, ammo or health is MOVE_TO, as before; harvesting crops is HARVEST; bringing something to a place or a person is DELIVER
intents.DELIVER: the bot carries something to a place or to a person: bring me the wood, take the wheat to the barn, put the eggs in the crate, carry the planks over here, give me the seeds, store the tools in the shed, drop the logs by the wall. Fetching the thing first is part of the order. A plain 'come here' is FOLLOW_ME
intents.BUILD: the bot builds or places a piece from its build menu: build a wall, put up a fence, place a barricade here, build a ramp up to the roof, set up a watchtower, lay a foundation, put in a door, make a crate, build cover. The item is what to build, as the player names it, also a piece the menu may not have ('build a pillar': the game answers that it has none). Taking cover behind something is TAKE_COVER; 'build cover' / 'put up some cover' is BUILD
intents.REPAIR: the bot repairs or strengthens something built or damaged: fix the wall, patch that hole, repair the fence, mend the gate, reinforce the barricade, fill the hole in the wall, seal the breach, reinforce that wall (as defenders do before a fight). Repairing the car is REPAIR too
intents.DEMOLISH: the bot takes down a structure: tear down the fence, demolish that wall, dismantle the watchtower, remove the barricade, knock down the shed, take apart the ramp. Blowing a way into a room through a wall is BREACH ('breach the wall', 'open the wall'); shooting at a wall is OPEN_FIRE
intents.SEE_THING: the player asks the bot whether it SEES something: the thing the player points at, looks at or names, or anything at all (do you see that?, can you see him?, see that guy?, do you have eyes on the door?, do you see the blue stairs?, can you spot him?, you got a visual on that?, are you seeing this?, do you see anything?, do you see any enemies?). It is a question, and the bot only answers it: it does not turn, move or shoot. Turning to look is LOOK_AT ('look at that'); going to look whether a place is clear is CHECK ('see if it's clear', 'go see what's there'); telling the bot what the PLAYER sees is a callout, NONE ('I see him', 'I see two on the roof'); asking whether the bot sees the player is SEE_ME
intents.SEE_ME: the player asks the bot whether it sees the PLAYER (do you see me?, can you see me?, see me?, am I in your view?, do you have eyes on me?, can you see me from there?). The bot answers; it does not turn to the player (LOOK_AT_ME) or come (FOLLOW_ME)
intents.SMALL_TALK: social talk to the bot that asks for no action: greetings and goodbyes (hello, hey buddy, good morning, see you), how it is (how are you?, how's it going?, what's up?, are you okay?, you still there?), thanks and apologies (thanks, thank you, cheers, sorry, my bad), questions about the bot itself (who are you?, what's your name?, are you a bot?, do you like this game?), and banter (tell me a joke, I'm bored, talk to me). The bot answers briefly. A question about the fight or the map is not small talk ('where are they?', 'how many are left?' are NONE); praise of what the bot did is PRAISE; with an order in the same line it is that order ('hey, cover me' is COVER_ME). A bare 'hi' or 'hi there' is not seeded here: speech-to-text hears the player's 'hide there' that way (TAKE_COVER)
intents.PRAISE: the player praises the bot or what it just did (nice shot, good job, well done, great work, nice one, nice kill, you're the best, you're awesome, good bot, that was amazing, great teamwork). The bot takes it, briefly; nothing else happens. A bare 'good', 'great', 'perfect', 'nice' or 'okay' that answers the bot is YES; praise with an order in the same line is that order ('nice shot, now follow me' is FOLLOW_ME); thanks are SMALL_TALK
intents.KILL_YOURSELF: the player tells the bot to kill itself or to die, as a joke or an insult (kill yourself, go kill yourself, shoot yourself, commit suicide, suicide, go die, just die, drop dead, end yourself, off yourself, kys, self destruct, blow yourself up, frag yourself). The bot refuses with a joke and does nothing. Killing an enemy is ATTACK ('kill him', 'kill them all'); 'don't die' / 'stay alive' / 'you'll die there' are NONE
intents.NONE: not an order to the bot: an information callout about enemies, chatter, a question, a complaint, or an order the bot has no intent for. A negated order is WAIT ('don't breach'); 'don't shoot' / 'don't fire' is the order HOLD_FIRE and 'don't move' is HOLD_POSITION. A report that the player or the team is under fire ('we're taking fire', 'I'm pinned down', 'I'm suppressed') is a callout: NONE, not SUPPRESS, HOLD_FIRE or HELP. What the player says they do themselves ('I'm jumping down') is not an order either. 'Roger' / 'copy' / 'got it' only acknowledge: NONE. What the player answers to the bot's question is YES / NO / MAYBE / DONT_KNOW. A going-on that names no way, side or place ('keep moving', 'keep going', 'continue', 'continue moving', 'keep it moving') is NONE: what the bot should go on with is in the talk before it; with a way named it is MOVE_TO. What the player says THEY do on the farm or the building ('I'm planting the carrots', 'I'll build the wall') and reports ('the wheat is ready', 'the fence is broken', 'we're out of wood') are NONE. Social talk to the bot ('how are you?', 'hello', 'thanks', 'who are you?') is SMALL_TALK, praise ('nice shot') PRAISE, asking whether the bot sees something SEE_THING or SEE_ME, and telling it to kill itself KILL_YOURSELF; a callout of what the PLAYER sees ('I see him') and questions about the fight ('where are they?') stay NONE

modifiers.timing: now | on_signal -- 'on_signal' when the player says to do it on their call / when they say go / on three; otherwise 'now'. 'On my mark' / 'at my mark' is NOT a signal: 'mark' is the player's marker on the map (see reference 'pin'), so 'check at my mark' is 'now'. 'Wait for my mark' is a signal 'On my goal' is 'on my go' misheard: a signal
modifiers.reference: pin | this | other | none -- how the line points at the place the BOT must act on. 'pin': the line names the player's marker ('my pin', 'the ping', 'my marker', 'on my mark', 'where I marked'). 'this': it points with this / that / these / those / here / there ('this wall', 'that window', 'over there', 'check that room'). 'other': the order is about the OTHER one of two things (the other door, the other window, the other angle). 'none': everything else -- a place that is only named ('the east window', 'the stairs') is 'none'. If two apply: pin, then other, then this. A pointing word that is about the player's own place or the enemy's does not count: 'I'll hold here, you take the north door' is 'none'
modifiers.target: the place on the map the BOT must act on for the order's first action -- go to, watch, open, throw at, shoot at, hide behind... -- as {object, qualifier, zone, direction, unknown_modifier}. object: one of the map's objects or null; qualifier: one of the map's qualifiers or null (also when the player named it without saying the object, e.g. 'push main' = door / main, 'take blue' = stairs / blue; a bare compass word with no object is qualifier only); zone: the floor the place is on, or the floor itself when the order is about the floor, else null. direction: up | down | left | right | forward | back when the line gives the bot's action a direction, with or without an object ('go left' = direction left only; 'go down the stairs' = stairs + down; 'the door on the left' = door + left; 'check behind you' = back), else null. A direction that describes the object is that object's: 'the door behind you' = door + back, 'the window above you' = window + up. If the line gives both the side that tells WHICH object it is and a direction of movement, give the side: 'go up the stairs on the left' = stairs + left. A word that only belongs to a fixed phrase is NOT a direction: 'fall back' and 'back up' (retreat), 'hold up', 'move up' and 'push up' (advance), 'get down' (take cover), 'two left' (remaining), 'right now', 'go ahead' (permission). 'upstairs' / 'downstairs' stay the zones up / down, with no direction. The target is NOT the player's own position, NOT where the enemy is and NOT the place to leave: 'I'll take the north door, you take the south window' -> window / south; 'I'll go left, you go right' -> direction right. unknown_modifier: true when the player singles out one particular object with a word that is neither a map name nor a direction ('the back door', 'the side door', 'the blue door', 'the second window', 'the stairs at the back': 'back', 'rear' and 'side' said of an object name a part of the building, not a direction); then give the object and leave the qualifier null. 'the left window' is NOT unknown_modifier any more: window + direction left. For a callout or chatter (intent NONE) give the place or direction the line is about, if it names one ('two on the left' = direction left). All are null / false when the line names no place of the map and no direction (a marker, 'here', 'there', 'that wall'). For LOOK_AT the target is what the bot must look at ('look at the sofa' = sofa, 'look at that window' = window, 'look left' = direction left); for LOOK_AT_ME it is the player, who is not a place of the map: all null. For CHECK the target is what to check ('check the room in front of us' = direction forward, 'check your six' = direction back); for SUPPRESS where to fire; for HELP it is the player: all null. For JUMP the target is where to jump or what to get over or onto ('jump down' = direction down, 'climb up' = direction up, 'jump over the sofa' = sofa, 'climb on the table' = table); the place to jump off is the place to leave, so 'jump off the roof' has no target. The player's marker is not a place of the map: 'stay at my pin' has all nulls and reference 'pin'; 'the window by my ping' = window, reference 'pin'. For COME_BACK the target is the place to come back to, if the line names one. For CROUCH / PRONE / STAND_UP and for the four answers all null. For GET_IN / GET_OUT the target is the vehicle (object 'car') if the line names one; for REPEAT all null. An item to get is the target of MOVE_TO: object ammo, weapon or health ('go find ammo' = ammo; 'grab a rifle' = weapon; 'go get health' = health); 'armor' or 'amor' heard where ammo is meant is ammo. For GO_BACK and HELP_INTERACTION all null: the place is the bot's own earlier one, or the player ('go back' gives no direction). Zone 'inside': a line that sends the bot indoors with no place named has zone 'inside' ('go inside', 'get indoors', 'get in the building'); a named place keeps its own ('get inside the car' = car). A ramp is not a map object: 'go down the ramp' = direction down. For SWITCH_WEAPON and RELOAD all null: a weapon named is one the bot carries, not a place ('switch to your pistol' names no place; 'pick up the pistol by my pin', MOVE_TO, does). For the farmer's and the builder's ten the target is the place where the work is done: the field or bed to plant, water, harvest or till ('plant carrots in the north bed' = bed / north), the animals' pen to feed in, the place to gather from (COLLECT: 'get the honey from the hives' = beehive), the place to build at (BUILD: 'build a wall at the east door' = door / east), the structure to repair or tear down when it is one of the map's objects (REPAIR / DEMOLISH: 'fix the fence' = fence), and for DELIVER the place the thing goes to ('take the wheat to the barn' = barn; to the player: all null). The thing itself is the item (see item). A crop word that singles out a field or bed ('the wheat field', 'the carrot bed') is unknown_modifier.
modifiers.item: the thing the order acts on, for the farmer's and the builder's ten intents (PLANT_CROP to DEMOLISH), as the player names it: lowercase, the noun with the words that name its kind ('wooden wall', 'tomato seedlings', 'scrap metal'), without articles, numbers, possessives and amounts ('some', 'a few', 'two rows of', 'a bunch of'); null when the line names nothing the order acts on, or only a general word ('build here', 'water them', 'harvest everything', 'water the plants', 'harvest the crops', 'collect materials'). It is what was SAID, also a thing the game may not have ('build a pillar' = 'pillar'). Per intent: PLANT_CROP the crop or seeds planted; WATER and HARVEST the crop; TILL null; FEED the animals fed, not the food ('give the cows some hay' = 'cows'); COLLECT what is gathered or taken ('collect the eggs' = 'eggs', 'chop some wood' = 'wood', 'milk the cow' = 'cow'); DELIVER what is carried ('bring me the planks' = 'planks'); BUILD what is built; REPAIR and DEMOLISH the structure ('fix the wall' = 'wall'). One of the map's objects is never the item but the target ('water the north field' = target field / north, item null; 'fix the door' = target door, item null), except for BUILD, COLLECT and DELIVER, where what is built, gathered or carried is the item even when the map has the word ('build a fence' = item 'fence', target null; 'carry the crate to the barn' = item 'crate', target barn). For every other intent null

map.note: Every map of the game has these named places, and players use the names in orders and callouts. Doors and windows are named by compass side, plus one Main door; stairs are named by colour; furniture and floors by what they are. The farm and the building site add their places: fields and beds, the greenhouse, the barn, the coop, the beehives, the well, fences, trees, crates, building spots. Some maps also have teleports (portals): walking into one takes you to another part of the map.

objects.door: a door: the Main door, or the north / south / west / east door
objects.window: a window: the north / south / west / east window
objects.stairs: a staircase: the blue / red / yellow / white / brown stairs
objects.car: a car, a truck, a vehicle (a car can be driven; it is also cover)
objects.ammo: ammunition: where the bot can pick some up
objects.weapon: a weapon: a gun, a rifle, a pistol, a shotgun lying or spawning somewhere
objects.health: health: a medkit, a health pack
objects.field: a field: crops grow on it (the north field; fields and beds are named by compass side)
objects.bed: a garden bed, a plot, a row, a planter
objects.barn: a barn, a shed, a storehouse
objects.coop: a chicken coop, a hen house, a pen, a stable, a sty
objects.well: a well, a water tank, a pump
objects.crate: a crate, a box, a chest, a container
objects.foundation: a building spot, a foundation, a frame the builder works on
objects.teleport: a teleport, a portal, a teleporter: walking into it takes you to another part of the map

zones.floor_2: a second floor, if the player names one
zones.inside: 'inside': indoors, under a roof, relative: the planner takes the nearest way in where the player looks

directions.up: upwards: 'go up', 'up the stairs', 'look up', 'from above'
directions.down: downwards: 'go down', 'down the stairs', 'drop down', 'from below'
directions.left: to the bot's or player's left: 'go left', 'on your left', 'the left window', 'the door on the left', 'nine o'clock'
directions.right: to the right: 'go right', 'to the right', 'the right door', 'three o'clock'
directions.forward: ahead: 'move forward', 'push forward', 'straight ahead', 'in front of you', 'twelve o'clock'
directions.back: behind, backwards: 'step back', 'behind you', 'check your six', 'to the rear'

items.note: what a line names as the item: examples by kind, not a closed list (the game has its own catalogue; a line may name anything)
